For n≥4 and strictly increasing a_i with pairwise distinct four-element subset sums, points Q_i(t)=(a_i,a_i²+2t a_i) are a common translate by (−t,−t²) of points (a_i+t,(a_i+t)²) on a strictly convex parabola, so all are convex-hull vertices. A circle equation restricted to (u,u²) is a monic quartic with absent u³ term. Four such points become cocircular exactly at t=−(Σa_i)/4. At a quartet's critical time the restriction is Π(u−u_r), negative precisely between first/second and third/fourth ordered abscissas. Thus the empty disk criterion requires four indices of the form {i,i+1,j,j+1} with i+1<j; any other quartet has an intervening fifth site strictly inside. The eligible event is a single empty convex-quadrilateral flip; testing the fourth point against the circle through the first three determines orientation (i+1,j+1)→(i,j) with increasing t. Distinct four-sums isolate all events. Sum_{i=1}^{n−3}(n−i−2)=binom(n−2,2), from the right fan at t→−∞ to left fan at t→+∞. Every flip is the same Tamari cover orientation and the known maximal chain length equals this count. Independently used exact integer circle-polynomial signs for generic 5^i parameters on n=4,...,8, checked only the adjacent-pair quartets are empty, obtaining 1,3,6,10,15 events. Inspected frozen check_kinetic.py exact-rational implementation; this bounded check is corroboration, not the all-n proof.
